quote: “And now let us believe in a long year that is given to us, new, untouched, full of things that have never been, full of work that has never been done, full of tasks, claims, and demands; and let us see that we learn to take it without letting fall too much of what it has to bestow upon those who demand of it necessary, serious, and great things.”
source: Rainer Maria Rilke, Letters 1892–1910, to Clara Rilke, Capri, 1 January 1907 (trans. J. B. Greene and M. D. Herter Norton, 1945)

evidence.where: The Greene and Norton translation as reproduced verbatim by WIST Quotations, which cites the Norton edition scan at p. 253; the German original is in Briefe aus den Jahren 1906 bis 1907 (Insel, 1930). I did not open the scan itself.
evidence.edition: Letters of Rainer Maria Rilke 1892–1910, trans. Jane Bannard Greene and M. D. Herter Norton, W. W. Norton, 1945, p. 253
evidence.locator: Letter to Clara Rilke, Capri, 1 January 1907

reason: The full published sentence in the named translation, from the letter the proposal names; the CFL wording “And now we welcome the new year” is a paraphrase and was rightly replaced by the curator.
